diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\Vert A\Vert^{-1}A=U^\top V$ be the decomposition given in Lemma
it admits a Cholesky decomposition $I_n-A^\top A = LL^\top $ with $L\in \f R^{n\times s}$

issues.failure_explanation: The constructed instance uses $V=[A/\|A\|;L^\top]$. Here $\|A\|$ is in general an irrational algebraic number, and $L$ is a Cholesky factor of a rank-deficient matrix, so it involves square roots. For integer inputs such as the biclique matrices $-M$, the output cone $\wt Q=VQ$ therefore has irrational entries. It cannot be computed exactly in polynomial time in the bit model. The proof only establishes equality of optimal values and of solution sets. It gives no argument for polynomial-time computability, which an NP-hardness reduction requires.

failure_location.quote: Then, $\SV(A,P,Q)$ reduces in polynomial time to $\MA(\wt P,\wt Q)$ where $\wt P:=UP$ and $\wt Q:=VQ$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize by a rational $c\ge\|A\|$ so that $I-A^\top A/c^2$ is rational and positive definite. Then show that it admits a rational factorization $LL^\top$, possibly in a larger dimension, computable in polynomial time, for example via $LDL^\top$ plus sum-of-squares representations of the pivots. Finally, verify that the solution correspondence survives the change of scaling.
issues.overall_effect: The NP-hardness of $\MA(P,Q)$ (Corollary cor:angles_cones_NPhard and the corresponding abstract claim) is not established as a polynomial-time reduction.
issues.title: Claimed polynomial-time reduction SV→MA requires irrational data (spectral norm, Cholesky factor)
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is likely recoverable, but recovering it needs a new contained argument (rational encoding of the lifting) rather than a local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Observe that $-\Vert A\Vert\leq \langle u,Av\rangle\leq\Vert A\Vert$ for all feasible pair $(u,v)$ of $\SV(A,P,Q)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Suppose $P=\R_+g$ and $Q=\R_+h$ with $0\le g^\top Ah<\|A\|$. Then both cones have one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times1$ nonnegative matrix, yet the optimal value is $g^\top Ah\neq\|A\|$. The correct condition is single generators with $g^\top Ah=\|A\|$.

failure_location.quote: since it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition with: $p=q=1$ and $g_1^\top Ah_1=\|A\|$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated preprocessing test for excluding $\lambda^*=\|A\|$ (needed before applying cor:saddle_ConeSV) is wrong as an equivalence.
issues.title: False characterization of the case $\lambda^*=\|A\|$
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction; no result depends on the wrong direction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be a local minimum of $\MA(P, Q)$ with $u \neq -v$ in dimension $n\le 3$
the minimum over the optimal values of $\MA(\f R_+g_i,Q)$ and $\MA(P,\f R_+ h_j)$ over all $i,j$ correspond to the maximum angle of $\MA(P, Q)$

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary assumes $u\neq-v$, but the prose drops this hypothesis. Counterexample in $\R^3$: take $P$ and $-Q$ to be cones over two triangles forming a star of David. Then $P\cap(-Q)\neq\{0\}$, so the maximal angle is $\pi$, attained only with $u=-v$. No generator $g_i$ lies in $-Q$ and no $h_j$ lies in $-P$, so every generator subproblem has value $>-1$. The claimed reduction gives the wrong value.

failure_location.quote: Corollary~\ref{cor:local_minimum_angles_have_generators_in_dim3} tells us that any solution $(u^*,v^*)$ of $\MA(P, Q)$ in dimension $3$ or less contains at least a generator.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the reduction only after excluding $\lambda^*=-1$ (checkable via the Case 2 preprocessing). Otherwise, return $-1$.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed polynomial-time procedure for $n\le3$ is incorrect when $P\cap(-Q)\neq\{0\}$.
issues.title: Dimension-≤3 reduction to generator subproblems ignores the excluded case $u=-v$
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing case, which is already handled by existing preprocessing, restores the claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To guarantee convergence, we restart the scheme when the objective increases

issues.failure_explanation: The cited two-block result applies to the relaxed problem over convex balls. That problem has stationary points that are not critical pairs of SV, e.g. $(u,v)=(0,0)$ with zero gradients. The implemented subproblems instead use the nonconvex constraint $\|x\|=1$. No argument links limit points of either version to solutions of (d1). The extrapolated and restarted scheme is likewise claimed to converge without proof.

failure_location.quote: hence AO is guaranteed to have a subsequence converging to a critical pair

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the claim to empirical convergence, or prove that limit points are nonzero and satisfy (d1), e.g. using $\lambda^*<0$ and monotone decrease, and handle extrapolation separately.
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence guarantee of AO/E-AO (Algorithm alg:eao) to critical pairs is not established.
issues.title: Unsupported convergence guarantee for (E-)AO to critical pairs
issues.why_classification: The method is a heuristic; weakening the guarantee leaves its role and the numerical results intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For this reason, from now on, we assume that $\lambda^*<0$.

issues.failure_explanation: In the relevant regime $e_k<0$. Once the iterates stall ($e_{k-2}=e_{k-1}<0$), the test reads $0\ge\delta e_{k-2}$, which is always true. Because this test enters the while-condition disjunctively, the loop continues until $k=K$ regardless of convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The objective-based stopping criterion of E-AO is inoperative, so termination is governed only by $K$ and the iterate-change tests.
issues.title: E-AO relative-decrease stopping test never triggers for negative objectives
issues.why_classification: A local fix to the stopping rule; the method's output and guarantees are otherwise unchanged.
